Details:
Best-Match XF Resolution(Standard)
A page includes an XF without specifying exact variant.


When a page is translated, two key properties are updated: "translation status" and "translation date."
Description:
A custom 'best match variation' resolver selects the most appropriate XF variation at render time based on the page's path (country, language, region).
Resolution Priority

Country + Language (e.g., en-US)
Language-only
Regeion
Master XF
Fallback Rule
If no match found ? Master XF is rendered.

•	The component accepts only the XF parent folder path; it resolves the variation automatically based on context.
•	All available variations are listed under the parent XF folder and named per region/language/country conventions.
•	These are manually created variations, not MSM live copies.
•	Default fallback is always the master variation.
•	These Translation  properties help the system decide whether to display a translated experience fragment or default to the English version if a translation is not available.
Key Points/Business Needs:
Two XF Authoring Models
1.  Standard XF Model

Flat structure
Variants by region / country
Used for marketing content
2. Division-Based XF Model (Forms only)

Additional division/ folder in XF path
Division selected via form properties
Used to support: Different backend endpoints (Eloqua, GCMS)
Solution:
- This is a customization that TF has built to allow for MSM kind of structure for XFs (as MSM in XF is not supported in AEM Sites).
- In DA Authoring, XFs are similar to site pages and therefore same multiple-level inheritence MSM strcuture can be applied to XF content. Therefore, this feature will not be required in DA Authoring.

Details:
Regional Container 

(This is not Specific to XF)
Description: The Regional Container component allows authors to explicitly target a block of content at one or more specific countries, including countries that do not exist in the MSM hierarchy. This allows Belgium, for example, to receive a custom XF block even though it inherits the UK page.
Key Points/Business Needs:
1.	Supports comma-separated country targeting — allows combining countries from multiple regions in one configuration.
2. Allows page-level inheritance (UK page) to remain intact while providing block-level country customization.
Solution:
Customization:
This feature will can be provided with a custom block (similar to how its built in AEM Sites, today.)

Description: This allows authors to explicitly specify a country, language, and XF ID rather than relying on the automatic best-match resolver. This provides a direct override capability at the component level.
Key Points/Business Needs:
1.	Authors manually specify country + language + XF path.
2.	Bypasses the automatic best-match variation resolution logic.
3.	Used for specific cases where the automatic resolution would not select the correct variant.
4.	Limited to a single country/language per component instance
